newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends higher on export talk, oil down.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends higher on export talk, oil down.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures closed firmer on Wednesday, supported by rumors China bought soymeal and by ideas cash demand remained strong, pit sources said.
Soyoil was lower on speculation increased soymeal demand would lead to a surplus of soyoil.

"There was a lot of commercial buying in the early part of the day but late in the day Cargill started buying puts," said Roy Huckabay, vice president of LIT, a division of First Options. "That might have been responsible for breaking the market down late."
Talk China was looking for soymeal was deemed supportive.
Huckabay and others said they could not confirm the business was done but some trade sources said it was likely China was buying South American soymeal.
The spot May soymeal set a contract high at $303.00 per ton, topping the previous high of $300.00 set on Tuesday.
Soymeal also drew strength from gains in soybeans tied to news the U.S. agricultural attache in Brazil cut its estimate for Brazil soybean production to 26.5 million tonnes.
Soymeal ended $3.50 to $1.30 per ton higher with July up $1.30 at $293.80 while soyoil ended 0.33 to 0.17 cent per lb lower with July down 0.25 at 24.84 cents.
Soyoil continued to struggle with the belief that demand for soymeal would lead to increased stockpiles of soyoil. Demand exists for soymeal, but soyoil usage levels have been lagging.
Commercials were said to be strong buyers of soymeal early. Cargill Inc bought 400 lots July, Continental Grain bought 300 July and ADM bought 200 May and 100 July.
Funds were also said to be buyers with Griffin Trading a buyer of 400 lots July. Prudential Securities bought 300 July and SAK Futures bought 400 July.
In soyoil, Rosenthal Collins was the featured seller of at least 2,000 lots July soyoil. Iowa Grain sold 300 July.
Cargill Inc bought 600 July and 100 August and Smith Barney bought 300 December and 100 July.
O'Connor and Co spread 800 lots October/December soymeal at $9.00 to $9.50, premium October.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT at 23,000 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume 24,332 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 21,000 lots, against Tuesday's 20,381.
